description: Python data visualization package built on matplotlib: simple chart functions, figure composition via Panel and Grid, and a global configuration system with predefined themes
rules: Target datachart 1.x. Pre-1.0 names were removed, not deprecated: use AXIS_SCALE (not SCALE), COLOR_NORM (not NORMALIZE), value_format (not valfmt), show_values (not show_heatmap_values), stats.pearson (not stats.correlation), config.update/config.reset (not update_config/reset_config), and save_figure(fmt=...) (not format=)

Import chart functions from datachart.charts; Panel, Grid, Annotate, save_figure and stats from datachart.utils; config from datachart.config; constants (THEME, FIG_SIZE, SHOW_GRID, LEGEND_LOCATION, ...) from datachart.constants

Chart data is a list of dicts, one per record, and each chart expects its own keys: LineChart x/y, BarChart label/y, ScatterChart x/y (optional size, hue, annotation), Histogram x, BoxPlot/ViolinPlot/SwarmPlot label/value. Check the chart's guide for the keys of other charts
A list of record lists draws several series. Name them with a list of subtitles; subplots=True gives each series its own axes
There is no pandas DataFrame input. Pass df.to_dict("records") with the columns renamed to the chart's keys
Every argument after data is keyword-only. An unknown parameter or constant value raises an error rather than being ignored

Set global style with config.set_theme(THEME.X), config.update(...) or `with config.using_theme(...)`. Per-chart overrides go in style={...} with theme keys such as plot_line_color. Prefer these over editing the matplotlib axes

Every chart returns a DatachartFigure, which is a matplotlib Figure. Panel overlays finished figures on shared axes; {"figure": fig, "y_axis": "right"} puts one on a second y-axis. Grid arranges figures in cells, with nested lists as rows. A Grid can sit inside another Grid but not inside a Panel
Save with save_figure(fig, path, fmt=[...]). fig.show(interactive=True) needs the datachart[interactive] extra
Docs index: https://eriknovak.github.io/datachart/latest/llms.txt. Append index.md to any page URL to get it as markdown
